title: Atomicize billing credits for fragmented live streams with out-of-order attachments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Live streaming sessions can include interleaved fragments, late-attached binary payloads (attachments), and client retransmits. Our current metering pipeline credits tokens pessimistically at fragment arrival and finalizes on session close, which can double-count or omit charges when fragments arrive out-of-order or when attachments increase token-length after an initial fragment was already credited. This causes customer billing discrepancies and quota enforcement holes for bursty clients.
background: We see sporadic billing complaints from customers using websocket streaming with attachments (image-to-chat, voice chunks). Existing tickets address edge reconciliation but rely on ad-hoc heuristics. This task aims to implement an explicit atomicization and finalization protocol in the metering pipeline so per-session credits are deterministically aggregated, deduplicated, and reconciled even with replays and out-of-order frames.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a streaming session with a client that splits input across multiple frames. 2) Send a short text fragment, then upload an attachment metadata frame that increases token estimate. 3) Simulate client reconnect and resend an earlier fragment. 4) Observe server metering logs and customer invoice/usage ledger; current behavior sometimes credits both the original and re-sent fragments or never updates credits to include the attachment.
impact: customer_impact: high; manifests as overcharges or undercharges and quota bypass for burst reconnects. Affects Hosted API and Dedicated customers using streaming endpoints. Leads to customer support load and SLA risk.
proposal_summary: Introduce a session-scoped provisional-credit layer that: (a) records all fragment deltas with strong idempotency keys, (b) tracks attachment token deltas separately, (c) exposes a deterministic finalization step triggered by session terminal events or time-based watermark to atomically commit or roll back provisional credits to the global ledger. During failover, a monotonic session checkpoint (server-assigned) will be used to reconcile duplicates.
design_decisions:
- Use server-assigned session_id + fragment_seq + deterministic fragment_hash as idempotency key.
- Provisional credits are kept in an append-only session store (Redis stream or Kafka partition) and compacted by checkpoint.
- Finalization will compute the max observed token tallies for input and output per session and write a single net delta to the billing ledger.
- Rate limiting and quota checks will consult provisional totals for enforcement but only decrement persistent quotas on finalization; provisional quota reservations will be bounded by a low-time TTL to prevent resource lock.
technical_work_items:
- Add fragment metadata parsing to gateway to populate fragment_hash and fragment_seq.
- Implement provisional_credit append-only store and compaction worker.
- Implement finalizer that atomically writes net delta to billing ledger with idempotency guard.
- Modify quota enforcer to read provisional totals and enforce soft-deny when provisional exceeds quota; translate soft-deny to hard deny on finalization if still over quota.
- Add backfill job to reconcile existing open sessions older than 24h.
- Update metering schemas and PRs + unit/integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end test where out-of-order fragments + attachment results in exactly one committed ledger delta matching final token tally.
2) Replaying the same fragment (duplicate idempotency key) does not change committed credits.
3) Quota enforcement does not allow persistent quota bypass when clients reconnect; provisional reservations expire cleanly on TTL.
4) No customer reports of duplicate charges in repro harnesses; synthetic billing audit passes for processed test sessions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency key generation, integration tests simulating reconnects and attachment late-arrival, chaos test injecting reordered fragments, regression test comparing historical billing mismatches on a staging dataset. Include load test to validate compaction worker under 10k concurrent sessions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the provisional store and finalizer behind meter_v2 flag. 2) Deploy compaction worker in canary with 10% of traffic. 3) Enable on a specific customer sandbox and run parallel billing audit for 48h. 4) Gradually increase traffic to 100% after 72h if no discrepancies. 5) Run reconciliation backfill for stale sessions. 6) Remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Metering finalization success rate (target > 99.9%).
- Count of duplicate idempotency key collisions (should be zero).
- Drift between provisional totals and committed ledger (alert if > 0.1% of tokens per hour).
- Side-effect: increase in quota-related soft-deny events during rollout (dashboard).
schema_and_contract_changes: Add fields to metering event schema: session_checkpoint (int), fragment_hash (string), provisional_token_delta (int), attachment_token_delta (int), finalization_id (string). Update downstream ledger write API to accept finalization_id for dedupe.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Provisional reservations could cause false quota holds and poor UX. Mitigation: keep provisional TTL small (30s by default), use soft-deny UX path on streaming clients. Risk: Compaction worker lag may delay finalization causing delayed billing — mitigate by autoscaling compactor and setting SLA for finalization latency.
notes: PM requested that billing transparency logs be made available to customers for contested invoices; added as follow-up (low priority). Also coordinate with Security for schema changes to ensure no PII is persisted.
